brief: Tells in plain sentences what a median-polish fit and its rule report found, without computing a single number of its own.
detail: Every number in the prose is read from the fit (the common value, the effects, the residual scale, the sweeps) or from a finding's message. IsHonest proves it on the story itself: each number in the text must be one the sources carry. The story has a paragraph on the fit, one on the effects, one on the findings when there are some, and a verdict. There is no language-model face on purpose, since templated prose reads well enough. Build it with StzTukeyStoryQ(oFit, oReport) after oFit.Polish().
receiver:
oFit = StzTukeyFitQ([ [ 11, 12, 13 ], [ 21, 22, 23 ], [ 31, 32, 33 ] ])
oFit.Polish()
o1 = StzTukeyStoryQ(oFit, StzTukeyReportQ("exact", [ oFit ]))
